props.gloss_en: one who wishes to accept upon himself the complete yoke of the kingdom of Heaven should relieve himself, wash his hands, don tefillin, recite the Shema and pray -- and this is the complete kingdom of Heaven
whoever relieves himself, washes his hands, dons tefillin, recites the Shema and prays -- Scripture credits him as if he built an altar and offered a sacrifice on it
as it is written: 'I will wash my hands in purity, and I will go about Your altar, Lord' (Ps 26:6)
Rava: does the master not hold that [such a one is] as if he immersed?
since it is written 'erchatz' (I will wash), and not 'architz' (I will wash [my hands])
one who has no water to wash his hands wipes his hands with earth, with a pebble or with a wood-chip
Rava: is it written 'I will wash in water'? 'in purity' is written -- anything that cleans
Rav Chisda would curse one who goes after water at the time of prayer
and this applies to the Shema
but for prayer one goes after [water]
and how far? up to a parasang -- and that is ahead of him
but behind him, he does not go back even a mil
and from it: it is a mil that he does not go back; less than a mil, he does go back
